first_difference.role: directional sensitivity only; no frozen permutation inference attached

all_five_descriptive.role: descriptive only because CHR and TOR have colony-code roster changes

ecological_interpretation: The strong long-term concentration of adult Adelie breeders among fewer colony-code components is not accompanied by a confirmatory change in island-level chicks per breeding pair after controlling adult abundance, persistent island differences and shared breeding-season effects. Thus the Palmer reorganization cannot currently be explained as either progressive reproductive deterioration or selective retreat into increasingly productive breeding space.
paper_implication: The adult breeding distribution reorganizes strongly while this independent reproductive-output endpoint does not track concentration detectably. This narrows the likely mechanism away from a simple contemporaneous breeding-success pathway and toward other life stages or state variables, including adult survival/recruitment, snow/terrain constraints, dispersal/site fidelity or predation that affects colony occupancy without a detectable island-level productivity signature.
interpretation_boundaries: Non-confirmatory association is not proof that breeding success is constant or irrelevant.
Island aggregation was required because colony-level chick-dataset breeding-pair denominators fail a hard biological-coherence audit.
The first-difference negative coefficient is not promoted over the frozen circular-shift primary result.
No causal terrain, snow, predation or survival mechanism is identified here.
next_gate: Use prospectively frozen terrain/snow-exposure predictors and species life-history contrasts to test whether terrestrial breeding constraints act differently in Adelie, chinstrap and gentoo penguins.
